name: Tilly chat #1 — share context (vegetarian, lives in Toronto)

body.message: Hey Tilly — quick context: I'm a Laurier student in Waterloo. I'm vegetarian and trying to stop spending so much on Wednesday afternoon DoorDash. Help me out.

reply.body:
Hey. Got you — Laurier, Waterloo, vegetarian. I'll remember all of that.

The Wednesday DoorDash thing is worth taking seriously. Delivery fees plus tips on a $12 meal can quietly turn it into $20+, and if it's a weekly habit, that's *$80–100 a month* just from one afternoon slot.

A few things that actually work for this pattern:

**The friction fix.** Delete the app from your home screen — just move it to a folder. You don't have to quit it. You just want one extra tap between the craving and the order. Most impulse orders die in that gap.

**The Wednesday anchor.** What's usually happening Wednesday afternoon — class ends, you're tired, there's nothing ready? If I know the trigger, I can help you plan around it. Even batch-cooking one thing Sunday (lentils, rice, whatever) that you know is waiting kills the craving before it starts.

**The ceiling.** If you still want to use DoorDash sometimes, I can help you set a mental ceiling — say, $15 all-in. That reframes it from a habit into an occasional thing.

Tell me more about what Wednesday afternoon looks like and I'll get more specific.
